comuneros-revolt-new-granada.research_focus: the 1781 Comunero revolt in New Granada, townspeople and peasants from Socorro marching toward Bogota
comuneros-revolt-new-granada.scene: A long column of townspeople and farmers in ponchos and wide hats marches along a mountain road toward a distant colonial city, pikes, machetes and a few muskets raised.

inconfidencia-mineira-plot.research_focus: the Inconfidencia Mineira conspiracy in Vila Rica, Minas Gerais, and Tiradentes
inconfidencia-mineira-plot.scene: Conspirators in late eighteenth-century coats lean over a candlelit table in a shuttered room of a hillside mining town, one man glancing toward the door as if they are already betrayed.

haitian-revolution-uprising-begins.research_focus: the August 1791 slave uprising on the northern plain of Saint-Domingue and the Bois Caiman ceremony
haitian-revolution-uprising-begins.scene: At night, enslaved men and women gather in a forest clearing under a storm sky while sugar plantations burn on the plain below.

narino-prints-rights-of-man.research_focus: Antonio Narino's secret printing of the Declaration of the Rights of Man in Bogota
narino-prints-rights-of-man.scene: A man in an eighteenth-century waistcoat works a wooden hand press by lamplight in a cramped back room, a stack of freshly printed sheets beside him, the pages shown blank or from behind.

gual-espana-conspiracy.research_focus: the 1797 conspiracy of Manuel Gual and Jose Maria Espana at La Guaira, Venezuela
gual-espana-conspiracy.scene: Spanish soldiers burst into a harbour-town house at La Guaira, seizing conspirators of mixed backgrounds around a table, ships at anchor visible through the window.

toussaint-louverture-captured.research_focus: the 1802 arrest of Toussaint Louverture by General Leclerc's officers and his deportation to France
toussaint-louverture-captured.scene: A dignified general in a bicorne hat is led under guard by French soldiers onto a ship's boat at the shore, his back straight, a warship waiting offshore.

portuguese-court-reaches-brazil.research_focus: the arrival of the Portuguese royal family and court fleet at Rio de Janeiro in 1808
portuguese-court-reaches-brazil.scene: A fleet of tall sailing ships enters Guanabara Bay beneath the Sugarloaf, and a royal party in court dress is rowed toward a crowded quay.

grito-de-dolores.research_focus: Miguel Hidalgo's call to arms at the parish church of Dolores in September 1810
grito-de-dolores.scene: Before dawn, an elderly priest in a cassock stands on the steps of a village church, arm raised, as parishioners with torches and farm tools crowd the square and the bell hangs in the tower above.

bolivar-named-el-libertador.research_focus: Simon Bolivar's triumphal entry into Caracas after the Admirable Campaign of 1813
bolivar-named-el-libertador.scene: A slim officer in a high-collared uniform rides into a colonial city plaza to cheering crowds, flowers thrown from balconies, seen from behind and in profile.

san-martin-crosses-andes.research_focus: the Army of the Andes crossing in 1817 under Jose de San Martin
san-martin-crosses-andes.scene: Soldiers and mules haul cannons up a narrow snowy pass between towering Andean peaks, an officer in a cloak on horseback watching from a ridge.

battle-of-boyaca.research_focus: the Battle of Boyaca in 1819 at the bridge over the Teatinos river
battle-of-boyaca.scene: Patriot cavalry and infantry charge across a small stone bridge over a highland stream as royalist troops in Spanish uniforms break and scatter.

bolivar-dies-santa-marta.research_focus: Simon Bolivar's last days at the Quinta de San Pedro Alejandrino near Santa Marta in 1830
bolivar-dies-santa-marta.scene: An empty hammock and a folded uniform coat hang on the veranda of a quiet hacienda house by the coast, an officer's sword laid on a chair, palms and the sea beyond; no figure shown.

spain-recognizes-mexico.research_focus: the 1836 Santa Maria-Calatrava Treaty in Madrid recognizing Mexican independence
spain-recognizes-mexico.scene: Two diplomats in 1830s frock coats sign a document at a gilded table in a Madrid palace salon, quill in hand, the paper seen edge-on.

duarte-founds-la-trinitaria.research_focus: Juan Pablo Duarte founding the secret society La Trinitaria in Santo Domingo in 1838
duarte-founds-la-trinitaria.scene: A small group of young men in 1830s dress clasp hands in an oath in a candlelit colonial room of Santo Domingo, one of them leading the vow.

dominican-independence-declared.research_focus: the night of 27 February 1844 at the Puerta del Conde in Santo Domingo
dominican-independence-declared.scene: At night, rebels with muskets and torches crowd around a massive stone city gate as a flag is raised above it.

narciso-lopez-invades-cuba.research_focus: Narciso Lopez's 1851 filibuster expedition landing in Cuba
narciso-lopez-invades-cuba.scene: Armed volunteers in mid-nineteenth-century dress wade ashore from boats onto a Cuban beach at dawn, a steamer offshore and palms ahead.

dominicans-rise-capotillo.research_focus: the Grito de Capotillo in 1863 that began the Dominican Restoration War
dominicans-rise-capotillo.scene: A handful of patriots on a grassy hilltop near the border raise a flag on a pole, machetes and rifles in hand, with forested hills rolling away below.

spain-leaves-santo-domingo.research_focus: the Spanish evacuation of Santo Domingo in 1865 after the Restoration War
spain-leaves-santo-domingo.scene: Spanish troops in kepis march in file down a harbour quay and board waiting ships while local people watch from the old city walls.

grito-de-yara.research_focus: Carlos Manuel de Cespedes at his sugar mill La Demajagua in October 1868
grito-de-yara.scene: On the grounds of a sugar mill, a planter in a linen suit rings the plantation bell before a crowd of men he has just freed, who take up machetes.

virginius-affair.research_focus: the capture of the steamer Virginius by the Spanish warship Tornado in 1873
virginius-affair.scene: A Spanish warship closes on a fleeing side-wheel steamer on a rough sea, smoke pouring from both funnels, with the Cuban coast on the horizon.

protest-of-baragua.research_focus: the 1878 meeting at Mangos de Baragua between Antonio Maceo and General Martinez Campos
protest-of-baragua.scene: Under a grove of mango trees, a tall rebel general stands firm before a seated Spanish general and his staff, his officers behind him refusing the terms.

marti-founds-cuban-revolutionary-party.research_focus: Jose Marti organizing Cuban exiles in New York and Tampa in 1892
marti-founds-cuban-revolutionary-party.scene: A slight man in a frock coat, seen from behind, addresses a packed hall of exiled cigar workers in 1890s dress, a flag hung on the wall behind him.

grito-de-baire.research_focus: the 1895 uprising in eastern Cuba and Jose Marti's landing at Playitas
grito-de-baire.scene: Mounted rebels in straw hats with raised machetes ride out of a village in the eastern Cuban hills at the start of the uprising, mountains behind.

antonio-maceo-killed.research_focus: the death of Antonio Maceo at San Pedro, near Punta Brava, in December 1896
antonio-maceo-killed.scene: Rebel horsemen gather in silence around a riderless horse in a field near Havana, a general's hat lying in the grass; non-graphic, no body shown.

treaty-paris-spain-cedes-colonies.research_focus: the signing of the Treaty of Paris in December 1898 ending the Spanish-American War
treaty-paris-spain-cedes-colonies.scene: Diplomats in 1890s frock coats sit around a long table in an ornate Paris salon as one signs, the papers seen edge-on, a chandelier above.

cuba-becomes-republic.research_focus: 20 May 1902, the transfer of power and the raising of the Cuban flag at the Palace of the Captains General in Havana
cuba-becomes-republic.scene: Crowds in 1900s straw boaters fill a Havana plaza as a flag rises on a palace flagpole and another is lowered, seen from below; no identifiable faces.
